Thanks, received and adding routing internally. Short summary of next steps: 

1) We will place an administrative evidence hold on the specified identifiers (90 days) — this prevents automated deletion and snapshot pruning across hosted/dedicated/private modes.
2) Security will prepare an export bundle (logs, request payloads, outputs, access logs); estimate 48-72 business hours for the first export and then incremental exports on request.
3) We will provide redaction options and a playbook (attached) that outlines reversible pseudonymization vs irreversible scrub.

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@crenshawhealth.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence hold + requested retention window for incident CH-20280601

Sara / Hannah / Rachel —

Thanks. Technical details below to help you decide on redaction approach and to set expectations for exports. 

Scope: request IDs map to request-level artifacts stored in (a) request logs (control plane), (b) inference payloads and generated outputs (ephemeral GPU runtime with optional caching), (c) embeddings and cached KV entries when "persisted" is enabled for long-running sessions.

What we will do for the 90-day evidence hold by default:
- Suspend automated deletion for matching request IDs across retention pipelines and ensure snapshots are flagged.
- Mark related storage objects with a hold tag to prevent lifecycle rules from expiring them.
- Include all access logs (token usage, IP, service account) in the export bundle.

Redaction options (tradeoffs):
1) Field deletion (hard delete of PHI fields) — irreversible, minimal re-identification risk, recommended when PHI should not be retained. Operationally we remove fields from stored payloads and scrub backups where feasible; note: truly purging all historical backups can take longer and may require separate workflows for cold backups.

2) Irreversible redaction (cryptographic shred) — we replace values with non-reversible hashes and remove plaintext; good when you need to retain structure (e.g., message length, token counts) but not PII/PHI. This is irreversible and satisfies most regulator expectations for deletion.

3) Reversible pseudonymization (tokenization) — replace identifiers with reversible tokens stored in a KMS-protected lookup. Pros: allows re-association for legal needs. Cons: higher long-term risk and usually not acceptable when a customer wants deletion for privacy law compliance. Requires KMS/HSM control and explicit retention policy.

Embeddings & model artifacts: embeddings created from customer inputs are by default treated like derived artifacts. For hosted customers, embeddings are stored in region with configured residency. We can:
- Delete embeddings matching request IDs (recommended if the customer needs removal),
- Pseudonymize embedding keys (less common), or
- Freeze them behind the evidence-hold tag (do not delete until lift).

Backups & snapshots: our automated backups might capture artifacts outside the active store. The export will include pointers to snapshots; full purge of snapshot copies can take up to 30 days depending on storage tier. We will mark snapshots for expedited purge if Crenshaw elects irreversible deletion, but timeline varies.

Export timeline: initial export (logs + payloads) 48-72 business hours. Full forensic export including backups/snapshots ~5-10 business days.

Audit trail: we will produce CSVs of access events and a signed manifest file (SHA256) for chain-of-custody.

Questions for you (choose preferred path):
A) Place hold only and later decide redaction method (we will retain artifacts as-is),
B) Place hold and commit to irreversible redaction at day 90,
C) Place hold and perform reversible pseudonymization (requires signed customer instruction and approval from legal).

If you confirm path B/C we will prepare a schedule and scope-of-work.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Sara —

Thanks for laying this out. Crenshaw's instructions captured in the attached PDF are sufficient to initiate the hold. For contract/audit purposes, please confirm which of the three options Priyom outlined you want us to schedule at the 90-day mark (A/B/C). Once you confirm, I will create an internal runbook ticket (Jira:SECOPS-2147) and a DocuSign approval if reversible pseudonymization is requested.

Quick notes for your team: 
- If you choose B (irreversible redaction), we will provide a certificate of deletion and an exported manifest. Expect snapshot purges to be batched and completed within 30 days following the deletion commit.
- If you choose C, please provide the list of authorized re-identification contacts and confirmation of KMS key ownership/rotation policy.

Action items: 
- Sara: confirm A/B/C by EOD Thursday (8 Jun).
- Hannah: I will record the hold and create the export task once Sara confirms.
- Priyom: prep the initial export template; include access logs and generated outputs.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
